text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed mostly easier with front month March losing $0.70 to close at $312.20 per tonne, while October gave up $0.20 to close at $304.70 per tonne. There was no fresh news to influence prices. Raw sugar futures in New York settled higher in quiet dealings. Front month July added 9 points to close at 10.88 cents/lb, while October closed 6 points higher at 10.72 cents/lb. Fundamentally players continue to await news on the more than 360,000-tonne delivery taken by Cargill. Traders are unsure whether the sugar will be weighing on the market or whether there is a destination.

TURKEY - Sugar imports in July 1996 amounted to 128,707 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 78,608 tonnes. This brought total imports in the 1995/96 season (August/July) up to 905,553 tonnes against 191,885 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1995/96 were France with 265,001 tonnes whites against 18,403 tonnes, Mexico with 127,596 tonnes against nil, the United Kingdom with 86,865 tonnes, up from 11,353 tonnes and the USA with 54,562 tonnes compared to 3,313 tonnes.

Turkey also imported some raw sugar for refining with Brazil (29,599 tonnes vs nil), Cuba (28,000 tonnes vs nil) and France (24,276 tonnes vs nil) being the main origins. Sugar exports in 1995/96 dropped sharply to 4,837 tonnes, down from 181,394 tonnes in 1994/95. The major country of destination in 1995/96 continued to be Iran with 1,764 tonnes whites, down from 57,241 tonnes.

CHINA - Sugar imports in March 1997 amounted to 20,146 tonnes, raw value, down from 64,288 tonnes imported in March 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1996/97 (September/March) up to 478,759 tonnes against 1.234 million tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 1.944 million tonnes against 2.907 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in September/March 1996/97 were Australia with 253,793 tonnes raws against 351,995 tonnes, Cuba with 132,590 tonnes compared to 168,953 tonnes and Thailand with 43,382 tonnes, down from 248,953 tonnes.

The largest supplier of white sugar was South Korea with 21,158 tonnes, up from 17,118 tonnes. Sugar exports in March 1997 amounted to 15,104 tonnes against nil in March 1996. This brought cumulative exports in September/March 1996/97 up to 195,256 tonnes against 577,863 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 830,203 tonnes against 540,004 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in September/March 1996/97 were Pakistan with 62,499 tonnes whites against nil, Saudi Arabia with 57,482 tonnes, down from 142,350 tonnes and Hong Kong with 27,090 tonnes compared to 78,925 tonnes.

Pakistan bought one cargo of white sugar at $351 a tonne, trade sources said. Further details were not immediately available. According to trade sources China sold 3 to 4 cargoes of 13,000 to 14,000 tonnes of white sugar to Pakistan for July delivery at around $370 per tonne, c&f Karachi. Pakistan prefers Chinese packing, along with bigger grains and drier sugar and is willing to pay up to a $10 premium for it. An invitation to supply 400 tonnes of sugar as European Union food aid to Angola has been published by the Commission in the official journal released on May 6. The deadline for tenders for shipment to the World Food Program of 'a' or 'b' white sugar, eligible for a periodic refund, will close on May 19, it was said.
